Viewforth · Investment memo · Sdiptech (SDIP.B-SE) · 31 October 2026

Sdiptech: a cleaned-up acquirer whose EPS now compounds at a mid-teens rate, but whose share price over the next 18 months depends on the multiple; add to the position after the Q4 2026 proof point, not before it

Written 31 October 2026 for Richard. The share price is SEK 254.8 (28 October 2026); the Financial Analyst's model prices returns from SEK 256.40 (22 October 2026). Money is in SEK millions unless stated. "Model EPS" is the Financial Analyst's definition throughout (set out in the end notes); any other EPS basis is named where it is quoted.

0Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The recommendation
Add to Sdiptech after the Q4 2026 cash proof point on 10 February 2027, not before it, and size the position for the volatility of the multiple rather than for the earnings.
Why the reward is skewed upwardsModel EPS compounds at 15% to 17% a year, about a third of FY2027's EPS increase is already contracted, and every acquisition closed is a visible upgrade to consensus. The earnings leg alone is worth about +28% to December 2027.
What can go wrongA Riksbank-led de-rating of the serial-acquirer cohort; a weak Q4 cash release that pauses acquisitions for two quarters; and, less likely, a UK recession and a sharply weaker pound arriving together.
The trigger on 10 February 2027Q4 2026 cash conversion above 100% with leverage at 2.6x to 2.7x: add. Cash conversion below 90% with leverage at 2.8x: wait, because acquisitions and the upgrade stream pause.

What the company is. Sdiptech is a small Swedish serial acquirer that has just completed a sixteen-month reset under a new chief executive and a returning chief financial officer. The group has core sales of about SEK 4.9bn from about 35 units in 13 countries, and 49% of its sales are in the UK.

The reset sold eleven service-heavy units plus Metus at 6.7x EBITA, took a SEK 500m impairment, redeemed the preference shares, refinanced the bonds from STIBOR (the Stockholm interbank offered rate) +4.90% to STIBOR +2.00%, cut leverage from 3.39x to 2.80x, and restarted acquisitions at about 6x EBITA upfront. The group that remains sells only products, earns adjusted EBITA margins of 20% to 21% and a gross margin of 59% to 60%, returns 13.6% on capital employed, and carries net debt of 2.90x to 2.95x adjusted EBITDA including earn-outs, against a 3.0x policy ceiling.

Key messageAdjusted EPS was flat at SEK 11 to 13 from FY2022 to FY2025 while revenue grew 48%. The three drags on EPS (share dilution, a seven-fold rise in interest and acquisition prices of 9x EBITA) are gone, so model EPS now compounds at 15% to 17% a year on EBITA growth of 12% to 14%.

The case in brief. The forecast needs nothing heroic to deliver that compounding. Organic growth normalises from 13% to 5% to 7%, the adjusted EBITA margin rises only 0.9 points in four years, and the company buys SEK 90m to 100m a year of acquired EBITA from free cash flow at about 6.5x. On those assumptions model EPS rises from SEK 15.27 in FY2026 to SEK 27.96 in FY2030.

About a third of FY2027's EPS increase is already contracted: the 2026 acquisitions annualise, the divested units leave the base and the refinancing is done. Consensus does not model unannounced acquisitions, so each closing is a visible upgrade worth about 0.7% of EPS per SEK 10m of acquired EBITA. The shares trade at 13.5x 24-month-forward earnings, their ten-year median, after a 46% rise in nine months.

The five insights that matter most.

1
The earnings leg of the case is well founded and modestly under-reflected by consensus; the multiple is where both the return and the risk lie. Like for like, the model's EPS for the businesses Sdiptech already owns equals DNB Carnegie's. The FactSet "consensus" (SEK 14.06, 17.66 and 19.19 for FY2026 to FY2028) is the median of two brokers on two different EPS definitions: DNB adds back the amortisation of acquired intangibles (purchase price allocation, or PPA, amortisation) and Nordea appears not to. The FactSet median therefore forecasts nothing in particular. The real gap between the model and the sell-side is the unannounced acquisitions, worth about 5% of FY2027 EPS and 7% of FY2028 EPS. That gap closes deal by deal, which makes it a dated, company-controlled upgrade stream, but a small one. The model's +84% return to December 2027 at the guideline multiple of 19.22x comes about three-fifths from the multiple and two-fifths from earnings. At the ten-year 75th-percentile multiple (16.1x) the return is about +54%; at the ten-year median (13.3x) it is about +28%.
2
Low operating leverage is the most useful single fact in the case, and it cuts both ways. Organic sales grew 11% and 13% in Q2 and Q3 2026, while organic EBITA grew only 5% and 6%. Three items explain most of that gap: about SEK 50m a quarter of near-zero-margin truck-chassis pass-through revenue at Hilltip, which management confirms ends in Q4 2026; a fixed-price rail project overrun at Mecno, which runs through Q4 2026; and a deliberate cost build in Water & Bioeconomy. The underlying incremental margin is about 25%. The first half of 2027 should therefore show organic EBITA growing faster than organic sales for the first time since 2023, which would disprove the "structural cost pressure" reading that RedEye leans towards. The same low operating leverage means that volume is not the lever for EPS: a point of organic sales growth is worth only about SEK 0.23 of EPS. The levers are capital allocation and the finance line.
3
Leverage, acquisitions and EPS form one system, and the next two quarters are the point at which that system is most constrained. Leverage of 2.90x to 2.95x against a 3.0x policy ceiling means that no acquisition of size can close before the seasonal Q4 cash release. Cash conversion was 134% in Q4 2025 and 62% in Q3 2026. If Q4 2026 cash conversion is above 100% and leverage prints at 2.6x to 2.7x on 10 February 2027, the acquisition engine can run at SEK 100m of acquired EBITA a year while leverage still falls about 0.3x a year, because EBITDA growth adds SEK 400m to 500m of debt capacity a year. If cash conversion is below 90% and leverage prints at 2.8x, acquisitions pause for two quarters and the consensus upgrade stream pauses with them.
4
The macro risk lies in the Swedish listing, not in the Swedish operations. Only about 6% of sales are in Sweden. Yet a Riksbank rate rise (to 2.0% on 4 November 2026 and to 2.25% in February 2027 on the banks' consensus; SEB expects 2.50%) hits the shares in three ways at once. It raises STIBOR on the roughly 55% to 60% of the SEK 2.8bn of bank debt that is unhedged, at a cost of SEK 0.2 to 0.7 of EPS per 100 basis points. It tends to strengthen the krona, and a 10% move in sterling is worth SEK 83m of EBITA and SEK 0.9 to 1.7 of EPS. It also compresses the serial-acquirer multiple, which halved across the cohort in 2022. Over 18 months, that multiple will decide Sdiptech's share price more than its earnings will.
5
Sdiptech is a set of good businesses inside a second-tier group. The units hold regulated, mission-critical, proprietary positions (67% to 68% of sales are the units' own products) and earn margins of 20% to 36%. The group adds no scale, no procurement leverage and only partial pricing power, which arrives with a six-to-nine-month lag. Its 13.6% return on capital is well short of the 18% to 22% at Lifco, Addtech and Indutrade, because Sdiptech paid about 9x EBITA for its acquisitions in the last cycle. The valuation discount to the compounders (11.1x against about 15x 2027 estimated EV/EBITA) reflects what Sdiptech paid and what it earns, so the discount will close only as the return gap closes. Closing the return gap is a two-to-three-year job, not an eighteen-month one.

Where I differ from the market. I am more positive than the market on the earnings and more cautious than the market on the risks and on the multiple.

Phase and setup. The stock is turning up with its thesis broadening. It becomes "reinforcing" only once the first half of 2027 shows profit growing at least as fast as sales and the acquisition engine running inside the leverage ceiling. The setup is a clearing cause for concern in a medium-quality, low-cyclicality business. The multiple has already moved from the first quartile of its ten-year range to the median, and a serial-acquirer EPS-upgrader setup is now taking over from the clearing concern. The fit with that setup is clean in kind but late in timing.

The four judgements that move the shares most, with the arithmetic

The multiple judgement dwarfs every earnings judgement: a plausible error on earnings costs 2% to 7% of EPS, while a plausible move in the multiple is worth 15% to 55% of the share price.

Judgement 1: organic EBITA delivery in FY2027 (base case: organic sales growth of about 7%, an adjusted EBITA margin of 20.7%, organic EBITA growth of 7% to 8%).

A plausible miss is organic sales growth of 4% and a margin of 20.2%. The 3-point sales shortfall on about SEK 5.2bn of core sales is SEK 155m of revenue, which at a 22.5% drop-through is SEK 35m of EBITA. The 50-basis-point margin shortfall on SEK 5.8bn of revenue is SEK 29m of EBITA. Together the two shortfalls are SEK 64m, or 5.3% of FY2027 EBITA. After 24% tax and over 38.0m shares, the shortfall is SEK 1.28 of EPS, which takes FY2027 EPS to SEK 17.1: 7% below the model and roughly in line with the FactSet hybrid. Return on capital would then stay near 13.5% rather than reach 14%. The tests are organic EBITA growth in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 (base about 4% to 8%) and the Supply Chain & Transportation margin returning above 20% by Q2 2027.

Judgement 2: the acquisition engine at SEK 90m to 100m of acquired EBITA a year at about 6.5x (base case: SEK 90m in 2027 with half a year's contribution, then SEK 100m a year).

Suppose a weak Q4 cash release pauses acquisitions until mid-2027 and the year delivers SEK 50m of acquired EBITA instead of SEK 90m. The FY2027 contribution then falls from about SEK 45m to about SEK 12m of EBITA (SEK -33m, or SEK -0.43 of EPS, -2.3%). FY2028 loses SEK 40m of carry-over plus SEK 15m from a slower start to 2028 (SEK -55m, or SEK -0.70 of EPS, -3.3%). The direct EPS cost is modest. The indirect cost is larger: the consensus upgrade stream (about 1.5% to 2% a quarter) stops, DNB's forecast for the businesses already owned becomes the whole case, and the "engine restarting" narrative that carried the multiple from 9.5x to 13.5x loses its evidence. If the engine instead runs at 8x upfront rather than 6.5x, each SEK 100m of acquired EBITA adds about 25% less EPS (SEK 1.0 rather than SEK 1.3 a year).

Judgement 3: sterling and the finance line together (base case: a 1% translation loss from GBP/SEK in each of 2027 and 2028; net financial items of SEK -262m in FY2027).

A 10% weaker pound against the krona removes SEK 83m of operating profit, about 8% of core EBITA, and SEK 0.9 to 1.7 of EPS (5% to 9%). Sdiptech's currency hedges mature within twelve months, so a lasting move in sterling passes through to profit within a year. A Riksbank cycle 100 basis points above the base adds SEK 11m to 33m of interest (SEK 0.2 to 0.7 of EPS). The sterling risk and the interest-rate risk are correlated, because a Riksbank rise strengthens the krona and raises STIBOR at the same time. A combined move of 5% on sterling and 100 basis points on STIBOR costs about SEK 0.65 + 0.45 = SEK 1.1 of FY2027 EPS (-6%), taking FY2027 EPS to about SEK 17.3. The offset is that part of the debt is in sterling, so net debt measured in krona falls with the pound and leverage stays roughly unchanged.

Judgement 4: the multiple (base case: the guideline 19.22x at December 2027 on 24-month-forward EPS of SEK 24.60).

One turn of the 24-month-forward P/E is worth SEK 24.6 a share at December 2027, about 9.6% of today's price. From today's 13.5x, a move to 16.1x (the ten-year 75th percentile) is worth +SEK 64 (+25% on the multiple alone); to 19.2x (the 90th percentile) +SEK 140 (+55%); to 11.9x (the 35th percentile) -SEK 39 (-15%); and to 9.2x (the 10th percentile) -SEK 106 (-42%). Each of these moves dwarfs the earnings judgements above. The level of the multiple is company-driven: the discount reflects the 9x that Sdiptech paid and the 13.6% return it earns. The direction of the multiple over six months is driven by interest rates and by the cohort: the compounders' median multiple halved in 2022, and a short-seller report on Lifco in January 2026 opened a 21% discount in a day with no change to Lifco's numbers. The combination that matters most for the downside is Judgement 3 and Judgement 4 arriving together: a Riksbank rise that costs 6% of EPS and two turns of multiple would take about 25% off the share price with no change in the operating business.

1Tailwinds in the operating environment; absence of headwinds

The conclusionExternal forces help the earnings forecast and hurt the multiple: demand comfortably supports 5% to 7% organic growth, but only the structural third of the demand improvement is durable, and the rate-and-krona regime works against a small, levered Swedish acquirer.

Evidence. Demand is improving for three different reasons, and each reason has a different durability.

Organic sales growth accelerated for five quarters, from -4% in Q2 2025 to +13% in Q3 2026, against a ten-year average of about 6%. The regulated niches have dated multi-year drivers: the UK water industry's AMP8 investment period (Asset Management Period 8, GBP 104bn for 2025 to 2030), the EU rail communication standard due by 2027, and, for data-centre security, NIS2 (the EU's revised Network and Information Security Directive) and the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill.

The wider evidence is supportive. European manufacturing purchasing managers' indices (PMIs) were 52.9 for the Eurozone and 58.1 for Sweden in September 2026, and the organic growth of Lagercrantz (12%) and Röko (9%) confirms demand in niche infrastructure. The UK Autumn Budget of 28 October 2026 was benign, with a net fiscal tightening of 0.02% of GDP.

The headwinds are real, and most of them are dated.

Inference. External forces help the forecast and hurt the multiple. At the earnings level, current demand comfortably supports 5% to 7% organic growth, since the forecast needs only about half of the growth now being delivered, but demand gives no help to the margin. At the valuation level, a small, levered, many-part Swedish acquirer sits on the wrong side of a rising-rate, risk-off regime.

So what. The current 13% organic growth rate is not a run-rate. Organic growth of +7%, +11%, +13% and about +10% in the four quarters of 2026 sets tough comparisons, which will slow 2027 organic growth mechanically to about 7% even if demand holds. Q3 and Q4 2027 carry a further four-point headwind as the chassis pass-through revenue leaves the base. At the same time, reported growth jumps to about 13% from Q2 2027, as divested units leave the comparison and the 2026 acquisitions annualise.

Headline growth will therefore accelerate while organic momentum fades, and the market may read the organic slowdown as a warning. The slowdown is normalisation. Organic growth below 3% for two quarters would be a genuine warning.

Market against me. The sell-side (DNB Carnegie and RedEye) models 6% organic growth for 2027 and calls the deceleration "purely a function of tougher comparisons"; I agree. I differ on the data-centre exposure. No commentator connects the financing fragility of the data-centre theme to Safety & Security's 36% margin, which management itself calls unsustainable and which the model takes down to 31%. If hyperscalers pause their projects, Safety & Security and Energy & Electrification together lose SEK 30m to 50m of EBITA (SEK 0.6 to 1.0 of EPS), more than the model's margin normalisation assumes.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The strongest counter-case rests on the UK. The UK is 49% of sales, UK construction is weak (brick deliveries hit a forty-year low for July), public capital budgets may be frozen in cash terms, and the old company missed consensus in five of six quarters in the last soft-UK period (2024 to mid-2025). I would turn more positive on the environment if the Riksbank stopped at 2.0% and EUR/SEK held near 11.0. I would turn more negative if UK PMIs fell below 50 or if the timing of data-centre projects slipped at Eagle and Phase 3.

Score: 61, set by the Rater. Structural regulated demand (grid, electrification, data-centre power and security, UK AMP8 water, EU rail standard) reaches about 37% of EBITA and organic growth has accelerated to +13%, but part is a timing and pass-through recovery, the UK (49% of sales) is soft, cost inflation and wage rises hit fixed-price units, the data-centre leg's financing is fragile and a stronger krona trims translated profit; the forecast needs only half of today's organic pace, so a mild net positive. This keeps Richard's ruled 61 ('fine') and the group score of 60, between Linea Directa (63, a strong but advanced, concentrated cycle) and Instalco (58, a recovery that flatters the figures).

2Internally-driven corporate change forces; absence of problems

The conclusionThe internal change is the strongest part of the case. The actions have been delivered on time and at disclosed prices; the conversion of growth into profit and cash, which is what a compounder is paid for, is still to be proved, and the proof points are quantitative and dated.

Evidence: the people. The whole executive layer changed inside eighteen months. Anders Mattson became chief executive on 1 June 2025; he is an internal appointment who had run Supply Chain & Transportation since 2018. Bengt Lejdström returned as chief financial officer the same day; he previously worked at Lagercrantz and Intrum, and DNB calls him "a reassuring anchor". A new Head of M&A (mergers and acquisitions) joined from Essity. Four new business-area heads came, respectively, from Munters, Hiab and Alfa Laval; from Signify and Schneider; from ESAB; and from an acquired company (Anders Petré, founder of WaterTech, who has run Water & Bioeconomy since 1 October 2026). The chief executive admitted publicly that subsidiary oversight had been too loose, and moved the board to hands-on governance.

Evidence: the actions. The strategic review began within weeks of the new chief executive taking office. Within twelve months, eleven units plus Metus (together 15% of sales and 5% of EBITA, at a 7.4% margin) were sold at 6.7x EBITA. Further actions are under way: cost indexation clauses are being added to contracts after the Mecno overrun, and a working-capital programme (consignment stock, smaller production batches) targets working capital of about 20% of sales. The acquisition engine restarted at about 6x EBITA upfront with Rail Safety Systems (Netherlands), JLM Teknik (Denmark), and A.U.T. Wheels and Castors and VALE Engineering (UK). These acquisitions had added about SEK 75m of run-rate EBITA by October 2026 against a SEK 100m target, after SEK 50m in all of 2025.

The problems. The problems are specific, and all of them sit on the "proving" side of the reset.

  • Growth is not yet dropping through to profit. Organic EBITA grew 4%, 5% and 6% in the first three quarters of 2026, against organic sales growth of 7%, 11% and 13%.
  • Cash conversion fell below the floor. Q3 2026 cash conversion was 62% (operating cash flow of SEK 143m against SEK 256m), below the 70% floor, and leverage rose back to 2.90x to 2.95x.
  • Water & Bioeconomy is unsettled. The business area has had three heads in about a year, and its margin fell from 23.8% in FY2024 to 20.3%; management calls the higher cost base "the new normal".
  • Oversight is thin. There is no internal audit function across about 35 units that run on different accounting systems.
  • Earn-out write-back gains roughly doubled. The gains rose to about SEK 90m in nine months of 2026, from SEK 48m in all of 2025. The 2025 gains are now traced to GAH's postponed fleet orders (a timing effect, since reversed); the 2026 gains are unattributed.
  • Executive ownership is thin. The chief executive held 23,003 shares plus 125,000 warrants at end-2025; the non-executive directors other than the chairman hold about 0.06% of the capital.
  • The restart concentrates risk. The new acquisitions deepen the UK and winter-weather exposures rather than diversifying them.
  • Three large holders sold into the rally. Handelsbanken Fonder cut its holding from 9.33% to 5.56% of the capital during 2026, Blacksheep from 6.91% to 3.64%, and Vulcan Value Partners (6.60% at end-2025) had sold its entire holding by the time of the October 2026 prospectus. The founder holds 5.31% of the capital and 15.34% of the votes.

Inference. The change forces are the strongest part of the case. The change has travelled through every layer: from people, to choices, to actions, to operating metrics (organic growth; return on capital up from 12.0% to 13.6%; leverage before the Q3 acquisitions), and into the sell-side's FY2027 estimates (+7% over three months). The change has not yet reached the conversion of sales into profit and cash, which is exactly what a compounder is paid for. The reset is past "doing" and inside "proving", and the proof points are quantitative and dated.

So what. Credit the plan's actions (acquisition pace, refinancing, the working-capital programme) and discount its outcomes (margin repair, return on capital) by about a year against management's framing of 2027 as the "full potential" year. The model already applies that discount to Water & Bioeconomy, taking its margin to 21.3% by FY2028 rather than back to 23.8%. The model does not apply the discount to Mecno, whose recovery it books in H1 2027. The Mecno exposure is SEK 15m to 25m of EBITA (SEK 0.3 to 0.5 of EPS), and the Q2 2027 Supply Chain & Transportation margin will settle it.

Market against me. The narrative that Sdiptech is "the cleanest reset in the cohort" is accurate and widely held by the two public commentators. The market has not priced two things. First, the institutional selling is a completed overhang: the shares absorbed roughly 11 points of capital from three holders and still rose 46% in nine months, and liquidity has improved as a result. Second, the earn-out write-backs are a signal about the quality of acquired units. I read the completed selling as a positive, and the write-backs as the most useful disclosure gap to probe.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The management team is new, untested together and untested in a downturn, and the segment the chief executive ran from 2018 is the one with the 2026 cost overrun and mix dilution. I would mark the change forces down if Q4 2026 cash conversion is below 90%, if Water & Bioeconomy loses a fourth head, or if a write-back is traced to an acquisition made in 2024 or 2025. I would mark them up to the top decile if H1 2027 shows organic EBITA growth above organic sales growth and the SEK 100m acquisition pace inside 2.7x leverage.

Score: 79, set by the Rater. A complete, on-time reset through every layer (new CEO, returning CFO, new M&A and business-area heads; 15% of sales sold at 6.7x; SEK 500m impairment; preference shares redeemed; bonds refinanced from +4.90% to +2.00%; return on capital in pay) with the acquisition engine restarted at about 6x, which is growth on top of repair, already lifting return on capital from 12.0% to 13.6% and FY2027 estimates by 7% in three months; held below the top decile by present problems (organic EBITA lagging organic sales all year, Q3 cash conversion 62%, three Water & Bioeconomy heads in a year). Above 74 as Richard ruled ('too low') and near the group's 80, between Volex (82, self-made expansion with guidance raised) and NKT (77, funded change working but with an overrun).

3Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile, management

The verdictGood businesses, not yet a great group: the units earn upper-quartile margins, while the group earns a second-tier return because of what it paid for them.

Evidence: the value chain. Sdiptech's units sell complex, certified, mission-critical products directly to municipalities, infrastructure operators, fleets, hospitals and data centres. No customer is above 5% of sales, consumer sales are below 5%, and aftermarket and service are 27% of sales. Competitors in the niches are margin-first and benign: prices did not fall when volumes fell in 2024 and 2025. The one commoditised niche is electric-vehicle (EV) charging. Rolec (about 6% of EBITA) faces more than 60 UK suppliers and Chinese hardware at USD 25 to 40 a unit, but the price shock has already happened and Rolec is growing again on UK fleet demand.

Evidence: the market for acquisition targets. For an acquirer, the industry structure that matters most is the market for targets, and that market is very fragmented but slowly filling. About 25,000 profitable European small and medium-sized companies pass typical filters, Sdiptech's pipeline holds about 800, and the company screens about 500 a week. Competition is rising: Addtech bought two UK companies in October 2026, and the share of Nordic compounders' acquisitions made outside the Nordics rose from 28% to 61% over a decade. Private equity pays 8x to 12x for targets above EUR 50m but is largely absent below that size, and the weaker listed acquirers (Volati, Indus, Storskogen) have lost their acquisition currency for now.

Evidence: the business model and moats. The units' moats come from three sources. The first is regulatory and certification lock-outs (medical air, nuclear, fume cupboards, trackside equipment). The second is the asymmetry between the product's cost and the customer's cost of failure, reinforced by co-development: GAH's lighter units won Ocado's whole fleet. The third is proprietary product and software: own products are 67% to 68% of sales, and Safety & Security's shift to software and secure communications lifted its margin from 30% to 36%. The gross margin is about 59% to 60%. There is no group-level scale, procurement leverage or network effect; clusters of related units (cold chain, rail, lifting, road maintenance) are the intended substitute and are at an early stage.

Evidence: the financial profile. Revenue grew 31%, 13% and 1% in the last three years, mostly through acquisitions. Cash conversion was 81% over twelve months, but erratic by quarter (134%, 54%, 70% and 62%), and DNB's stricter free-cash-flow measure averages about 53%. Unit-level returns, excluding acquired intangibles, exceed 60%.

Evidence: management. Management is strong on actions and weak on disclosure below EBITA.

  • Ambition is peer-standard. The targets are SEK 2,000m of adjusted EBITA by 2030, more than 15% total EBITA growth a year and a return on capital above 15%. Lifco, Storskogen and Volati set the same numbers, and two of those three have missed them.
  • Strategy is right, and bold in execution. Management sold 15% of sales in one programme, took a SEK 500m impairment and priced a return-on-capital rule into pay.
  • Communication is clear on operations and poor below EBITA. One interim report carried three different EPS figures.
  • Chief executive pay is in the bottom quartile (SEK 4.98m).
  • Governance is prudent on paper, with two named gaps: there is no internal audit, and a non-independent former chief executive who is close to the founder sits on the board.

Inference. The units earn their margins from structural positions of the kind the market pays well for at Lifco and Halma. The group earns a second-tier return because of the price it paid in the last cycle (about 9x EBITA, against a Nordic median of 6x to 8x), and it converts cash erratically. Acquisitions at 6.5x upfront and about 8x total consideration yield about 12.5% pre-tax on the total price, which is below the group's 13.6%, so the acquisition engine barely lifts return on capital. Return on capital rises mainly through organic EBITA growth on a stable capital base and through working-capital release (about SEK 200m of one-off cash if the target of 20% of sales is met). The model has return on capital at 14% by the FY2027 report and at 15% only by 2030.

So what. The right forecasting stance is to hold segment margins where the units earn them, assume no group-level margin expansion from scale, and let all the compounding come from the price and pace of acquisitions and from the flat finance line. The fair multiple for this profile is in the mid-teens, not the 20x-plus of the premium compounders, until Sdiptech shows returns above 15% on new capital.

Market against me. The sell-side frames the case as closing a 35% valuation discount to the Swedish compounders (11.1x against about 15x 2027 estimated EV/EBITA). I agree that the discount is too wide for a cleaned-up portfolio; RedEye puts the justified discount below 25%. I disagree that the discount closes on momentum alone. The 7 October 2026 research finds that, across the cohort, the valuation gap tracks the price paid and the return earned, not the quality of the niches, so a discount closes only when the return gap closes. For Sdiptech that is 2028 to 2029, not 2027.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The strongest counter-case is that, at the unit level, Sdiptech's returns and moats are as good as Lifco's, and the market will anticipate the group-level repair once two or three quarters of return on capital above 14% are printed. A first year of acquisitions at 6x to 7x total consideration (not just upfront), disclosed deal by deal, would raise my view of the quality of the business model. An acquisition at 9x total consideration, or the margin of a second segment breaking down, would lower it.

Score: 56, set by the Rater. Units hold regulated, certified, mission-critical niches with 67-68% own products, no customer above 5% and margin-first rivals (20-36% unit margins, 59-60% gross margin), but the group adds no scale or procurement leverage, pricing power lags six to nine months, and the return on capital is 13.6% against 18-22% at Lifco, Addtech and Indutrade because it paid about 9x; new deals at 6.5x upfront and 8x total earn about 12.5% pre-tax, so new capital barely lifts returns. Figures.md's ROIC (-0.4%, p9) and gross margin (7.1%, p6) are impairment- and definition-distorted and I set them aside; the EBITDA margin (22%, p60) fits. Coherent with the groups (50-60) and Richard's ruled 56, between Helios Towers (60, unit economics strongly above reported returns) and Vodafone (55, a simpler, better business emerging).

4Conservative guidance; keeping expectations conservative; record of delivery and upgrades

The conclusionNear-term guidance is conservative and will mostly be met. The mid-term targets are a ceiling, not a base, so upgrades will show up as delivery above the guidance bands rather than as formal raises, which the market rewards less.

Evidence. The company gives no annual numerical guidance. Instead it sets building blocks, announced at the November 2025 capital markets day and reaffirmed at the Q2 and Q3 2026 reports, and 2026 is tracking them.

Management's informal commentary is cautious on margins and confident on activity. On margins, management calls Safety & Security's margin "not sustainable", says Mecno's overrun runs "through Q4", describes the Water & Bioeconomy repair as "not yet fully secured" and calls the higher cost base "the new normal". On activity, management expects capital allocation to "step up quarter by quarter", calls the acquisition pipeline "significantly strengthened" and presents 2027 as the "full potential" year. The sell-side calls management an "honest tracker" with "conservative tendencies".

The record of delivery. Recent quarters show sales beating consensus and the margin falling short; the older record is one of misses.

  • The last four quarters: revenue beat consensus by -2%, +3%, +7% and +7.5%, and organic growth beat DNB's forecast by six to seven points in each of the last two quarters. Adjusted EBITA beat by less than half as much, and the margin missed in every quarter (Q3 2026: 20.0% against a consensus of 20.9%).
  • The last three years: the old company mostly missed consensus (2024 to mid-2025), missed its organic EBITA targets in FY2024 and FY2025, saw FY2025 consensus EPS cut by 44.5% over twelve months, and halved its 2025 acquisition target.
  • Upgrades: the company has never raised a target. The nearest formal opportunity is the FY2026 report on 10 February 2027, and no capital markets day is scheduled before late 2027.

Inference. The guidance is of the useful kind for a modeller, and it is conservative in the near term: with organic sales growing at 10% or more, a 5% to 10% band for organic EBITA growth is realistic for profit and conservative for sales. The mid-term target is a ceiling, not a base. More than 15% total EBITA growth a year equals what the group achieved from 2022 to 2025 with equity issues, leverage above 3x and acquisition prices of 9x. The model has +14.1% for FY2027 and about 12% to 13% a year after that, reaching SEK 1.7bn in FY2030, 15% short of the 2030 ambition, which would need SEK 150m a year of acquired EBITA from 2028. The pattern of delivery (sales beating, margin short) is structural for now and is the right lean for 2027.

So what. Over the five reports to April 2028, I put the odds as follows.

  • About 65%: the building blocks are met and the targets reaffirmed.
  • About 15%: something is raised or added. The most plausible candidates are a faster acquisition pace, a dividend policy or a return-on-capital bridge at a late-2027 capital markets day, if leverage is near 2.4x with the engine already at SEK 100m a year.
  • About 20%: a building block is missed. The SEK 100m acquisition target for 2026 is more likely than not to be missed by SEK 5m to 25m, which the sell-side will excuse as timing.

The 2030 ambition is more likely to be quietly reframed in 2027 to 2028 than reached; I put the chance of reaching it at about 25% to 30%. That caps the "guidance upgrade" leg of the case while leaving the "delivery against conservative building blocks" leg intact. The non-binding ambition also removes a risk, because it does not force the company to overpay for acquisitions.

Market against me. The market treats the 15% EBITA growth target as the base case for 2027 (DNB: "2027 could be a strong year with 15% EBITA growth including recent acquisitions"). I expect FY2027 to be a near miss on the group base (+14%), which the company can present as met on the core base. I also expect the honest, building-block style of guidance to make "upgrades" appear as delivery above the bands rather than as formal raises, which the market rewards less.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The strongest counter-case is that a management team that has under-promised for sixteen months and now sees 13% organic growth could raise the organic band or the acquired-EBITA target at the February 2027 report; the team's humility is a choice, not a constraint. A formal raise, or disclosure of the total consideration for each acquisition, would move my score up ten points. A second cut to the acquisition target, as in 2025, would move it down.

Score: 37, set by the Rater. The old company mostly missed from 2024 to mid-2025, missed its organic EBITA targets in FY2024 and FY2025, halved its 2025 acquisition target and saw FY2025 consensus EPS cut 44.5%, and it has never raised a target; since the reset the building blocks are met and sales beat, but the margin missed consensus four quarters running and the SEK 100m 2026 acquisition block is more likely than not to be missed. Below 47 as Richard ruled on the two-to-three-year history and close to the groups (34 and 40), between Hexatronic (38, one beat that does not repair a weak two-year record) and Solid State (30, profit warnings and an unproven honest-tracker claim).

5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out scope, feedback loops

Key messageThe 2026 gap between organic sales growth (+13%) and organic EBITA growth (+6%) is mostly about SEK 50m a quarter of near-zero-margin chassis pass-through revenue, which management says ends in Q4 2026, plus the Mecno overrun. The underlying incremental margin is about 25%, so H1 2027 should show organic EBITA growing faster than organic sales for the first time since 2023.

Evidence: pricing power. Pricing power is real in the product niches and lagged in the service and project units. In the product niches, GAH's EBITA rose 76% after its acquisition on value-based pricing, Energy & Electrification held its margin at about 25% through component inflation, and Safety & Security's margin rose six points. In the service and project units, management admits a six-to-nine-month pricing lag: Water & Bioeconomy's margin fell 3.5 points as UK wages rose against fixed-price insurer contracts, and Mecno's fixed-price projects absorbed cost rises. At group level, price adds about 2 to 3 points of revenue growth a year and about nothing to the margin.

Evidence: operating leverage. A 60% gross margin and a semi-fixed staff cost of 28% of sales should give high drop-through. In practice, each of about 35 units staffs to its own two-month order book, so realised drop-through is 20% to 25% of incremental organic sales, close to the average margin, and volume lifts the group margin by only 0.1 to 0.2 points a year. The 10% drop-through realised in 2026 is mostly the result of pass-through mix and the Mecno overrun.

Evidence: financial leverage. Net financial items of about SEK 260m to 280m a year are roughly fixed in money, so they fall from about 27% of EBITA in FY2026 to about 14% in FY2030. Every 1% of EBITA is therefore worth about 1.27% of pre-tax profit in FY2027, and adjusted pre-tax profit grows about 1.2 times as fast as EBITA.

Evidence: cost-out scope. There is no cost-out programme and none is needed. Identified efficiencies (Mecno's overrun ending, the Water & Bioeconomy repair, procurement clusters, spare-parts pricing) are worth SEK 35m to 50m of EBITA by FY2028 and are already inside the model's margin path. Central costs are small and rising. The finance line is the largest reducible cost, saving SEK 12m to 15m a year from the refinancing.

Evidence: feedback loops. One reinforcing loop dominates, and several balancing loops constrain it.

  • The reinforcing acquisition-cash loop. Free cash flow of about SEK 580m to 900m a year after leases funds SEK 90m to 100m of acquired EBITA at 6.5x. The acquired EBITDA raises both cash flow and debt capacity: EBITDA growth of SEK 170m to 200m a year adds SEK 400m to 500m of debt capacity at a constant 2.5x leverage. The loop is worth 6 to 8 points of EBITA growth a year and about half of the EPS growth from FY2027 to FY2030.
  • The balancing loops. The seasonal working-capital trough binds from Q3 2026 to Q1 2027, and the leverage ceiling binds over the same two quarters. The earn-out schedule (SEK 159m to 162m in 2027 and SEK 392m to 436m in 2028 to 2029) absorbs 20% to 35% of free cash flow. Mix dilution from the fastest-growing, lowest-margin area costs 0.1 to 0.2 points of margin a year. The rates-and-krona loop and the price-cost lag loop complete the set.
  • A loop that works both ways. Earn-out write-downs cushion leverage in a downturn: earn-outs fall about 40%, or about 0.4x of EBITDA, if acquired profits stay flat. The same write-downs flatter reported profit while they last.

Inference. Revenue growth does lead to outsized profit growth at Sdiptech, but through the balance sheet rather than through the income statement. EBITA grows about 1.1 times as fast as revenue (mix and modest margin repair), pre-tax profit about 1.2 times as fast as EBITA (fixed finance costs), and EPS about 1.0 times as fast as pre-tax profit (no dilution beyond about 1.7% from warrants in 2028 to 2029). From FY2026 to FY2030, revenue compounds at about 11.5% a year, EBITA at about 12.7% and model EPS at about 16.3%. The last cycle had the same acquisition engine and produced flat EPS because interest rates rose, acquisition prices were 9x and shares were issued. The new cycle removes two of those three drags; interest rates remain the shared risk.

So what. The annual forecast is predictable, but the quarterly reading is treacherous. Volume errors move EBITA roughly in proportion and do not widen the range of EPS outcomes. A downturn's decremental margin is moderate at 25% to 35%: in FY2025, with core organic sales down 1%, the core margin held at 21.5%, and Lifco grew EBITA 7% in 2020 on organic sales down 5.8%. Quarter by quarter, however, pass-through deliveries make revenue and margin move in opposite directions for a single reason, so a sales beat and a margin miss can be one event, as they were in Q2 and Q3 2026.

Market against me. RedEye reads three quarters of gross margin below 60% (58.1% in Q3 2026 against its forecast of 61.4%) as cost pressure and lower incremental margins, possibly structural. I read the whole Q3 fall in gross margin (from 60.4% to 58.1%) as reproducible from about SEK 50m of near-zero-margin chassis revenue on a SEK 1.25bn revenue base, which management has confirmed ends in Q4 2026. The EBITA margin also fell only half as much as the gross margin, which is the signature of mix and not of cost pressure. If I am right, H1 2027 shows organic EBITA growth above organic sales growth, and the debate ends within two reports.

The market also under-weights the financial-leverage arithmetic. Nobody writes that a flat finance line turns 13% EBITA growth into 16% to 17% EPS growth, because the brokers carry about SEK -275m of net financial items for FY2027 against the model's SEK -262m.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The counter-case has three parts. Hilltip's "new larger road product segment" may mean that complete-vehicle orders recur. The post-divestment cost base may be structurally higher. And a Riksbank cycle 100 basis points above the base would turn the financial leverage against shareholders (SEK 0.2 to 0.7 of EPS) just as the earn-out schedule peaks. A Q1 2027 gross margin back above 60% would confirm my reading; a complete-vehicle order in Q3 2027 would weaken it.

Score: 47, set by the Rater. Operating gearing is weak for a 60% gross-margin model: about 35 units each staff to a two-month order book, so drop-through is only 20-25% (close to the average margin) and volume adds 0.1-0.2 points a year; pricing is real in product niches but lags in service and project units and adds about nothing to group margin. A roughly fixed finance line (27% falling to 14% of EBITA) and the free-cash-flow-funded acquisition loop amplify EPS, so EPS compounds about 1.4 times revenue (16.3% against 11.5%), below the Universe's typical twice, but the downside decremental is moderate (25-35%); an ordinary mix slightly below typical, coherent with Economic strength at 50.

6Forecast financials; scope for double-digit growth; higher growth and margins than the past

Key messageAbout a third of the FY2027 EPS increase (from SEK 15.27 to SEK 18.38) is contracted before 2027 begins: the 2026 acquisitions annualise, the divested units leave the base and the refinancing is done.

Evidence: the model of record. The forecasts of record are the Financial Analyst's model update 2.

The model's further assumptions are these. Organic growth in FY2027 runs at 9%, 7%, 6% and 6% by quarter. Acquisitions cost about 6.5x EBITA upfront and 8x in total, at EBITA margins of 23%. Currency costs 1% of revenue in each of 2027 and 2028. Working capital starts at 24.0% of revenue and falls 0.5 points a year to 22.5%. Capital spending is 3% of sales. Earn-outs paid are about SEK 300m, 182m, 263m, 314m and 145m for FY2026 to FY2030. Leverage on the company's definition, including earn-outs, is about 2.6x to 2.7x at end-2026, then about 2.4x, 2.1x, 1.8x and 1.5x.

The Financial Analyst's own cross-check runs EPS 1% to 2.4% above the model, on a lower share count. The cross-check's free cash flow runs SEK 40m to 50m a year above the model because of a definitional difference (non-cash earn-out unwinding and lease interest).

Evidence: against the past. From FY2019 to FY2025, revenue compounded at 19% a year, two-thirds of it acquired and partly funded with equity. The operating EBITDA margin rose from 16.8% to 22.0% through portfolio change. Net interest rose seven-fold and the share count rose 25%. Adjusted EPS on the brokers' basis went from SEK 13.16 in FY2023 to 11.45 and then 7.22 in FY2025, a figure polluted by the impairment; DNB's adjusted FY2025 EPS is SEK 13.30. Reported FY2025 EPS was SEK -2.18.

Inference. The next four years are a slower-revenue, higher-quality version of the last six. Revenue growth roughly halves, and EBITA growth runs a little below the 2022 to 2025 rate of about 15%, yet EPS growth is several times faster than the roughly flat EPS of FY2022 to FY2025, because the drags have gone. Margin progress runs at a third of the historical pace (+0.9 points over four years, against +5 points over six) because the portfolio lever is spent.

The scope for double-digit growth is therefore clear on EPS (mid-teens) and present but unspectacular on EBITA (12% to 14%). The scope for higher margins than in the past is nil at group level: the core margin was 21.5% in FY2025, and the model reaches 21.2% in FY2030. That absence of margin upside is a sign of the forecast's honesty rather than a weakness of the business.

So what. The FY2027 EPS bridge, from SEK 15.27 to SEK 18.38 (+SEK 3.11), shows that about a third of the increase does not depend on anything happening in 2027. The bridge is roughly as follows.

  • About +1.1, already contracted: the 2026 acquisitions annualising and the divested units leaving the base.
  • About +1.4 from organic EBITA growth of 7% to 8%: this includes about +0.4 from the reversal of Mecno's overrun and about -0.4 from Safety & Security's margin normalising.
  • About +0.5 from the 2027 acquisitions, with half a year's contribution.
  • About +0.3 from the finance line: the refinancing, and the absence of 2026's SEK 20m of redemption premia.
  • About -0.2 from currency.

From FY2027 to FY2030, model EPS rises a further SEK 9.6. About 40% of that increase comes from organic EBITA growth and margin repair and about 60% from acquisitions before their financing cost (about 40% net of the debt they leave unpaid); the finance line and the warrants roughly cancel each other out. Two drivers, both reported quarterly, carry about 95% of the change.

Market against me. Against the FactSet hybrid consensus, the model is 8.6%, 4.1% and 11.1% higher on EPS for FY2026 to FY2028, and 2.1%, 6.1% and 12.3% higher on revenue. Most of the FY2026 EPS gap and part of FY2027's is definitional. Like for like, on DNB's basis, the forecasts for the businesses already owned agree within 1% (SEK 19.6 against SEK 19.5 for FY2027), and with acquisitions included the model is about 5% above DNB for FY2027 and 7% above for FY2028. Against the company's own targets, the model sits below the 15% EBITA growth target and 15% below the 2030 ambition.

The apparent consensus "step" in the FY2027 EBITDA margin, from 23.0% to 25.3%, is an artefact of the FY2026 base: the FY2026 median mixes DNB's adjusted 25.3% with Nordea's 22.8%, which appears to include items affecting comparability. On adjusted EBITA, DNB models a margin gain of 50 basis points a year and the model 40 basis points for FY2027. I therefore agree with DNB on the shape of the forecast and disagree with the FactSet figures mainly on definition.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The strongest counter-case is that the model assumes two things the old company never had, acquisition prices of 6.5x upfront and a flat finance line, and that the out-years lean on about SEK 300m of acquired EBITA not yet identified. An earlier review weighted confidence in the forecasts at 70% for FY2027, 55% for FY2028 and 40% to 45% for FY2029 to FY2030, and I share those weights.

I did not change any forecast input. The base case already sets the margin below DNB's, the latest model update already raised the finance line and corrected a double count of working capital on acquired revenue, and my differences with the model concern the multiple, which is not a model input. I would lower the FY2027 margin by 10 to 20 basis points (SEK 0.1 to 0.2 of EPS) if Q4 2026 shows a Supply Chain & Transportation margin below 19%. I would raise FY2028 if the 2026 acquisition count reaches six or more.

Score: 90, set by the Rater. 16.3% sits just inside the 15-30% A band (consensus next-year growth is only 10.5%, p48, partly on definition). Placed at the floor because the growth is front-loaded (+20% in FY2027), comes from a flat finance line and about SEK 300m of acquired EBITA not yet identified rather than organic margin gain, and the group margin (20.3% to 21.2%) only returns towards the FY2025 core 21.5% rather than exceeding the past.

7Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Key messageThe FactSet "consensus" EPS is a median of two brokers on two definitions. Like for like, the forecast for the businesses already owned equals DNB Carnegie's, and the only real gap is unannounced acquisitions, worth about 5% of FY2027 EPS and 7% of FY2028 EPS, arriving at about 0.7% of EPS per SEK 10m of acquired EBITA closed.

Evidence: the upgrade mechanism. The mechanism is known and dated. DNB Carnegie states that acquisitions are the main driver of its revisions, because consensus includes only announced acquisitions; the Q3 2026 pair (A.U.T. and VALE) added about SEK 40m of EBIT and about SEK 0.5 of EPS. At SEK 20m to 25m of acquired EBITA a quarter, FY2027 consensus should rise by about 1.5% to 2% a quarter through 2027, and FY2028 consensus by more.

Evidence: the brokers' record and coverage. On this stock, the brokers have been too low on organic sales (DNB forecast 6% for Q3 2026 against an outcome of 13%, and RedEye raised its 2027 and 2028 sales forecasts by 5% after Q3) and too high on the margin. The brokers carry about SEK -275m of net financial items for FY2027 against the model's SEK -262m, a difference of about SEK 0.3 of EPS.

  • FactSet contributors: two. DNB forecasts EPS of SEK 15.1, 19.5 and 22.0 for FY2026 to FY2028 after Q3; Nordea forecasts SEK 12.1, 16.2 and 18.9.
  • Outside FactSet: RedEye forecasts SEK 15.85 for FY2027, because it charges acquisition financing and amortisation, with a base-case value of SEK 315 a share and a range of SEK 170 to 435.
  • Horizon: FactSet holds no consensus beyond FY2028. FY2029 and FY2030 exist only in RedEye's and DNB's models, so a fourth-year consensus will appear during 2027 resting on one or two brokers and, by convention, excluding acquisitions.
  • Investor commentary: none visible on X, on Swedish forums or in the financial press after the Q3 report.

Inference. Consensus is more likely to rise than fall over 18 months. It will rise in steps rather than as a trend, and by less than the gap to the FactSet median suggests, because about a third of that gap is definitional. My probabilities for FY2027 EPS by February 2028, like for like, are: higher by 3% or more, 60%; within 3%, 25%; lower by 3% or more, 15%. The probabilities for FY2028 are the same, with a wider range.

The upward drivers are larger and more certain than the downward ones, but the downward ones are external and correlated. The upward drivers are acquisitions, organic sales, the finance line, and the Q4 cash release, which would pull DNB's leverage path and its separate M&A scenario (SEK 366 a share) towards each other. The downward drivers are the margin (1% to 2% of EPS), currency (1% a year on growth, and up to 5% to 9% of EPS per 10% move in sterling) and interest rates (1% to 4%).

So what. Four narrative upgrades are available and not yet written. In order of value:

  1. The FactSet consensus is a hybrid, and the like-for-like sell-side forecast agrees with the forecast for the businesses already owned, so every acquisition is a visible upgrade against a base that is not as low as it looks.
  2. A third of FY2027's EPS increase is already contracted.
  3. The gap between organic sales growth and organic EBITA growth is transitory, and H1 2027 should show organic EBITA growing faster than organic sales.
  4. The Q4 cash release is the gate on the flow of acquisitions.

Each of these upgrades can be checked from the company's own reports within six months. The optical acceleration of reported growth to about 13% from Q2 2027 will read as momentum. Because so few analysts cover the stock, little is priced in either direction and little will re-price fast. One broker initiating coverage would be a narrative event in itself: SEB and ABG are named as covering Sdiptech but do not publish.

Market against me. On the dashboard (28 October 2026), sell-side momentum is pinned at B and the revision-momentum score is 12. FY2027 EPS is up 2% over one month, 7% over three and 8% over six, and the target price is up 10% over six months. The buy share is 100%, so breadth has nowhere to go but down and is not a useful signal here. I agree with the direction of revisions and think the market under-reads their size: the mechanism is contractual (about 0.7% of EPS per SEK 10m of acquired EBITA closed), and the Q4 report is the swing event. Revisions are best read through DNB's own series and RedEye's base case rather than through the FactSet median, because Nordea's figures are about 15% below DNB's on definition alone and any change of contributor moves the median without any change in the company.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The largest upgrade driver, acquisitions, is also the best known, so each step will surprise less than the last. If the Q4 cash release fails, the upgrade stream pauses exactly when the narrative needs it. A 2026 total of more than SEK 100m of acquired EBITA announced by February 2027 would raise my probability of upgrades to 70%; Q4 cash conversion below 90% would cut it to 40%.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, is likely met and reaffirmed rather than raised (about 15% odds of a raise, 20% of a missed block, the SEK 100m acquisition block likely short); consensus excludes unannounced deals, so each closing adds about 0.7% of EPS per SEK 10m of EBITA, and FY2027 EPS has about 60% odds of rising 3% or more, roughly 5% over the period against about 12% reported revenue growth (a ratio near 0.4-0.5, about the 60th percentile), with transitory drop-through and a contracted third of FY2027's growth as unwritten narrative upgrades but the Q4 cash release as a gate. Coherent with the group's 56, between Munters (66, record orders well ahead of consensus) and Teqnion (59, thin evidence of upward pressure).

Evidence: guidance and narrative. The targets were set in November 2025 and have been reaffirmed twice; nothing has been raised, and the near-term building blocks are being met at or above the floor. The narrative, "the cleanest reset in the cohort", is accurate and held by the two public commentators.

Evidence: sell-side momentum (pinned B). FactSet's FY2027 mean EPS is up 3.9% over one month, 7.3% over three, 9.6% over six and down 0.6% over twelve (range SEK 15.82 to 20.41). FY2028 is up 10.6% over six months. FY2026 is down 0.8% over one month and 12.6% over twelve. The cutting is therefore over and the outer years are rising. Broker targets range from SEK 313 to 342 (median SEK 313) and are up 10% over six months; the buy share is 100%.

Evidence: technical momentum (pinned A). The share price of SEK 254.8 is 12.1% above the 200-day average of SEK 227, which has risen in seven of the last twelve months; the 50-day average is SEK 253 and the 150-day average SEK 242. Relative strength is at the 79th percentile of the universe. The 52-week range is SEK 164.5 to 271.0, and average daily value traded is about USD 2.6m to 3.9m. Valuation is pinned at C: the P/E is at the 52nd percentile of its own ten-year history.

Evidence: peers. Among the dashboard's diversified industrial groups (28 October 2026), the reset sub-cohort is strong, the premium compounders are weak and the control case is broken. Lifco's weakness follows a short-seller report in January 2026 and a customer loss in October 2026, and its revision score is -8. Twelve-month returns inside the sector span 148 points, so sector membership explains little. Sdiptech's return has tracked its reset sub-cohort (+28% over twelve months) and its own events, not the sector.

Inference. The stock is technically extended at a moment when the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting digest reads the market regime as risk-off and broadening, with Momentum at Underweight and Fragility at Double Underweight. A small, levered, many-part Swedish acquirer sits on the wrong side of both readings. Three holders have sold roughly 11 points of capital into the rally and the market absorbed the selling, so that overhang is largely spent.

So what. Over the next six weeks, the dated events skew negative for the multiple and neutral to positive for the earnings. On the negative side are the Riksbank decision on 4 November, Indus's Q3 report on 12 November (the unwinding of its tungsten windfall, with read-across to the cohort) and the European Central Bank's rate pricing into 2027. On the positive side is any acquisition announcement: the company needs about SEK 25m more of acquired EBITA to reach its SEK 100m target. The next company-controlled positive event is the FY2026 report on 10 February 2027.

Market against me. I use the dashboard's momentum readings as given and differ only in how much weight to put on them. With two brokers, a 100% buy share and about USD 3m a day of liquidity, the "momentum" is a handful of institutions reading two research notes. The technical A therefore says more about the completed reset than about crowding, and good news travels slowly in this stock. I would not treat the 79th-percentile relative strength as a crowding risk in the way I would for a widely held name.

Counter-case and what would change my view. A 46% rise in nine months means that part of the reset is already banked ("a crisp setup fit is often a late one"). The one-month revision of +2% is slowing from +7% over three months. The Lifco precedent shows that the cohort can lose 16% in a day on a report nobody has read. A break below the 50-day average (SEK 253) together with a Riksbank rise would turn the technical reading; a third broker initiating coverage with a buy recommendation would strengthen the sell-side leg.

Score: 85, set by the Rater. Both measures are positive and just short of the top fifth, so B; FY2027 EPS +7% over three months (p85) and +9.6% over six, targets +10%, buys at p85, and the price 12% above a rising 200-day average and above its 50- and 150-day averages. Placed high in the band because no part is negative, but not moved to A: guidance has been reaffirmed rather than raised, the one-month revision is slowing, and peers are split (the reset sub-cohort strong, Lifco weak).

9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The verdictThe case is predictable at the operating level, moderately predictable at the EPS level and unpredictable at the share-price level.

Evidence: simplicity. Two drivers that the company reports quarterly generate about 95% of the forecast's EPS change: organic adjusted EBITA growth, and acquired run-rate EBITA (with EBIT and consideration disclosed for each acquisition). Those two drivers plus the finance line generate most of the change over the next 18 months. The margin micro-drivers are each worth 1% to 3% of EBITA and largely offset one another: Mecno (SEK 8m to 10m a quarter), Hilltip's pass-through (about 0.8 points of group margin), Safety & Security (SEK -20m to -30m), Water & Bioeconomy (SEK -5m to -10m for two to three quarters after each April wage rise) and the procurement clusters (SEK +5m to +15m).

Evidence: the range of outcomes. At 80% confidence, FY2027 model EPS lies between about SEK 16.0 and SEK 21.0, against the model's SEK 18.4 (about -13% to +14%); currency and interest rates account for about half of that width. The 5th and 95th percentiles are about SEK 14.5 and SEK 22. The skew is mildly negative against the model and positive against consensus. It is negative against the model because every external variable currently points the wrong way, the identified margin items are asymmetric (Safety & Security's normalisation is near certain and the only identified upside is smaller), and the acquisition pace is capped above by the leverage ceiling and open below. It is positive against consensus because consensus excludes acquisitions.

Evidence: fragilities and requirements. The forecast needs six things to hold.

  • A Q4 2026 cash release above 100%, as in Q4 2025 (134%).
  • Acquisition prices near 6.5x upfront and 8x in total. The 2024 acquisitions averaged 5.3x upfront and 7.9x in total; the long-run average was about 9x.
  • Adequate control of a faster acquisition pace. A nine-person executive team is doing six to eight acquisitions a year with no internal audit across about 35 units on different accounting systems. The Storskogen precedent is a SEK 30m due-diligence charge at Tungdykargruppen, followed later by SEK 600m of impairments.
  • An orderly roll-off of the interest-rate hedge book. About 40% to 45% of utilised credit is swapped, with maturities of one to 3.5 years and undisclosed strike rates, and the swaps are rolling off into a rising-rate cycle.
  • Funding for the earn-out schedule, which peaks in 2028 to 2029.
  • Acceptable visibility of subsidiaries, whose performance is visible only through UK Companies House filings that can be up to eighteen months late.

Evidence: suddenness and trackability. The fundamental risks are mostly slow and trackable from company disclosure, with two exceptions: an accounting or control failure in one unit, and the dual shock of a UK recession plus a sharply weaker pound while earn-outs fall due and hedges roll off. In the dual shock, the acquisition engine stops and the multiple falls to the cohort's 9x. The perception risks are more likely than the fundamental ones and similar in size; a break in the data-centre trade is a further perception risk that is not sized.

Evidence: sector and cyclical precedents. The cohort underperforms in five situations: when leverage meets a cycle (Volati, at 4.5x including preference shares, -77%); when the price paid outruns the return (Storskogen in 2021 to 2022, paying up to 10x); on windfall "false friends" (Indus); on contagion driven by opacity (Lifco); and on rate rises (multiples halved in 2022). Sdiptech's own cyclicality is low. Core organic sales fell 1% in FY2025 with the margin held, construction exposure has been exited, and the decremental margin is 25% to 35%, not the 40% to 60% of fixed-cost manufacturers. The demand of the largest segment is driven by replacement cycles and fleets rather than by construction. Sdiptech's cycle exposure is to the UK economy and to the pound, which makes it a currency cycle more than a volume cycle.

Inference. At the operating level the case is predictable: core EBITA in local currency lies within about plus or minus 6% of the FY2027 base. At the EPS level it is moderately predictable. At the share-price level it is unpredictable, because the multiple has ranged from 9.5x to 35.8x in five years and its direction over six months belongs to the Riksbank, the European Central Bank and the cohort's next shock.

The EPS basis is itself a risk to expectations. The company shows three EPS figures, FactSet four bases, and the two brokers differ by exactly the PPA amortisation per share (SEK 2.8 to 3.1). A "beat" or a "miss" at the EPS line will therefore be reported against a hybrid and mean little. The clean quarterly tests are adjusted EBITA by segment, cash conversion and leverage.

So what. Track the case in the company's own reported units. Each indicator below has a base level and a warning level. The one thing to watch that the disclosure does not give is which units generated the earn-out write-backs.

Market against me. The market's reading of case riskiness (pinned at C) matches mine. I differ from the drivers report on diffuseness: the report calls the driver set "moderately diffuse", whereas I call it diffuse at the level of anecdote and concentrated at the level of EPS, which is favourable for a forecaster. I differ from an earlier review on skew: that review called the FY2027 range of outcomes symmetric. I think the correlated external variables make the lower tail fatter than five independent sensitivities suggest, because a UK slowdown weakens sterling and organic growth together, and a Riksbank rise strengthens the krona and raises STIBOR together.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The strongest counter-case is that the decentralised portfolio limits every single-unit shock, the balance sheet has SEK 1.75bn of undrawn facilities and covenants at 3.25x and 4.50x against a 3.0x policy ceiling, and the next bond maturity is September 2030; on that view the riskiness lies in perception more than in fundamentals. A Q4 2026 report with cash conversion above 100% and leverage at 2.6x to 2.7x would move my riskiness grade one notch better. A Riksbank path to 2.50% with EUR/SEK at 10.70 would move it one notch worse.

Score: 46, set by the Rater. Two quarterly-reported drivers carry about 95% of the EPS change and the operations are low-cyclicality (core margin held at -1% organic in FY2025), but the FY2027 cone is about -13% to +14% with a fatter lower tail from correlated sterling, krona and STIBOR moves, leverage of 2.9x sits at the 3.0x ceiling for two quarters, the hedge book rolls into rising rates, there is no internal audit across 35 units with unattributed earn-out write-backs (about 5% odds of a control failure at -10% to -25%), the dual shock carries about 10% odds at -30% to -40%, and a multiple that has ranged 9.5x to 35.8x is exposed to cohort contagion. Between the groups' 44 and 64 and next to IMCD (49, about 3x leverage and dual-shock FX risk in a simple model), above OMV Petrom (44, sudden fiscal interventions).

10Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Key messageThe stock is turning up with its thesis broadening, one phase behind the dashboard's "Reinforcing" reading. The move to reinforcing is dated to the Q1 2027 report (late April 2027), if H1 2027 shows profit growing as fast as sales and the acquisition engine at SEK 100m a year inside 2.7x leverage.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule puts the starting phase at Reinforcing, on technical momentum of A, sell-side momentum of B and a 24-month-forward P/E of 13.5x. Against that reading:

  • The multiple has risen from 9.5x (March 2025) and 10.2x (September 2025) to 13.5x, the ten-year median, in thirteen months, and the shares have risen from SEK 173.7 to SEK 254.8.
  • FY2027 and FY2028 estimates have risen 9.6% and 10.6% over six months, after FY2025 estimates were cut by 44.5% over the previous twelve.
  • Guidance has been set and reaffirmed, never raised, and the margin has missed four quarters running while sales beat.
  • The first clean year of evidence for the product-only group (organic EBITA growing faster than organic sales, the engine at SEK 100m inside the ceiling, cash conversion inside the 70% to 90% corridor, return on capital near 14%) is 2027, and its first proof point is 10 February 2027.

The staircase ahead has three flights. The near steps are well founded and low in novelty: further acquisitions, the FY2026 report with a strong Q4 cash flow, relief at Mecno, and Petré's first actions in Water & Bioeconomy. The novel steps come in months 6 to 18: quarterly evidence of drop-through, return on capital rising towards 14% to 14.5%, possibly a first German platform acquisition, and wider broker coverage. The large, uncertain step comes in months 18 to 36: return on capital crossing 15%, leverage low enough for a first distribution to shareholders, and a re-rating towards the 14x to 16x of the mid-tier compounders. The Riksbank, Indus's report and the European Central Bank run against the near steps.

Inference. The stock has finished bottoming: the Q3 2025 "kitchen sink" brought the impairment, the divestment programme and a halved acquisition target. The stock has turned up on the completed repair, and the thesis is now broadening from "balance sheet fixed" to "engine restarting and growth returning". The stock is not yet reinforcing, because a reinforcing phase requires repeated delivery at the margin and cash lines and an upgrade cycle that has run for more than two quarters. The current cycle has neither a raised target nor a single quarter in which profit grew as fast as sales. The dashboard rule's "Reinforcing" is a reading of price and revision momentum; the fundamentals are a phase behind.

So what. The phase decides the fair multiple (topic 11): a turning-up, thesis-broadening stock whose forecasts are uncertain at the reported level warrants a multiple lower in its range than a stock in peak delivery. The phase also sets the catalysts. If H1 2027 shows drop-through and the acquisition engine on pace, the move from broadening to reinforcing would be dated to the Q1 2027 report (late April 2027). The market would then have about twelve months of reinforcing evidence before the 2028 to 2029 earn-out peak and the hedge roll-off test it. The risk of stalling is a Q4 2026 cash miss; the risk of collapsing is the dual shock, and that risk is low.

Market against me. The dashboard rule and the technical reading say Reinforcing; the sell-side's frame is "turning point, bluer skies ahead"; RedEye says the market's scepticism is warranted until organic profitability is proven. I sit between the brokers. The shares have earned the move from a first-quartile multiple to the median, and the next leg, from the median to the upper quartile, needs the 2027 evidence, not more of 2026's.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The counter-case is that momentum phases are self-reinforcing in thinly covered stocks with 100% buy ratings and a known upgrade mechanism, so the market may price the reinforcing phase before the evidence arrives. AddLife did exactly that: it restarted in early 2026 at 15x EV/EBITA and reached 18x by October on six acquisitions and 83% cash conversion. Two quarters of organic EBITA growth above organic sales growth, with leverage at or below 2.7x, would move my phase to Reinforcing; Q4 2026 cash conversion below 90% would move it to Stalling.

Score: 74, set by the Rater. The memo's Turning up with the thesis broadening is right and the computed Reinforcing runs ahead of the fundamentals: the bottom was the Q3 2025 kitchen-sink, estimates for FY2027 and FY2028 have risen about 10% in six months and the story is widening from repair to engine restart, but there is no target raise and no quarter of profit growing as fast as sales, and the 46% nine-month rise to the median multiple has banked part of the turn. Between AQ Group (78, Broadening with a margin target raised) and Kuehne + Nagel (72, early Reinforcing that is not fully backed).

11The fair multiple

The conclusionMy fair multiple over the next 18 months is about 16x 24-month-forward earnings, the ten-year 75th percentile, not the guideline's 19.22x. The 3.1-turn difference is worth about SEK 77 a share, about 30% of today's price, and it is the single largest judgement in the memo.

Evidence: the guideline and the history. The guideline fair multiple from the Phases page is 19.22x 24-month-forward earnings: the 90th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history (108 of 111 months used; three outlier months excluded), and 42% above today's 13.51x.

The stock reached 19x or more only in July 2020 and from November 2020 to May 2022 (peaking at 37.2x in August 2021): the compounder mania of near-zero rates and 30% revenue growth funded with equity. It traded at 8.3x to 10.1x through 2018 to 2019 and at 13x to 17x through most of 2023 to 2024. The five-year median is 14.2x and the two-year median 12.4x. On FactSet's basis, today's multiple of 13.8x is at the 43rd percentile of five years and the 80th percentile of two years.

Evidence: peers and brokers. On EV/EBITA the stock trades at 11.1x 2027 estimates, against about 15x for the Swedish compounder group and 18x to 21x for Lifco, Addtech and Lagercrantz (DNB, 26 October 2026). The brokers' targets imply about 16x to 17x our FY2027 to FY2028 earnings: DNB's SEK 340 applies a 10% discount to the compounders on 2027 estimates, Nordea's target is SEK 327, and RedEye's SEK 315 uses a 9.1% cost of capital.

Inference. The level of the multiple is company-driven, and the company has earned the move to its median. The guideline's 19.2x is the right multiple for a stock with four attributes: peak delivery, reinforcing evidence, low leverage and a benign rate regime. Sdiptech is one phase short of the first attribute, two years short of the third (return on capital at 15%), and in a regime that is the opposite of the fourth.

My fair multiple for the next 18 months is about 16x, the 75th percentile, for three reasons: the brokers' targets sit there; it is the mid-tier compounder level (14x to 16x) that a 14% return on capital and a running acquisition engine justify; and the stock traded at roughly that level in mid-2024, before the last downgrade cycle. Reaching 19x within 18 months requires four things together: the Q4 cash release, H1 2027 drop-through, SEK 100m of acquired EBITA inside 2.7x leverage, and the Riksbank stopping at 2.25%. Falling back to the median of 13.3x requires only that one of those four fails or that the cohort de-rates.

So what. The difference between the guideline and my view is worth about SEK 77 a share at December 2027 (3.1 turns on 24-month-forward EPS of SEK 24.60), about 30% of today's price. That difference is the single largest judgement in the memo, and it is a judgement about the rate regime and the phase, not about the company. If Richard shares the dashboard's Reinforcing reading, the guideline stands. If he shares mine, the fair multiple is 16x, and the model's return should be read at the 75th-percentile line in topic 12.
