Market against me. The market is at 13.5x, the brokers at 16x to 17x and the guideline at 19.2x. I am with the brokers on the level and below the guideline. I am above the market because I think the discount to the compounders is too wide for a portfolio that has shed its service units and is buying at 6x. I would caution against the brokers' framing of "a 10% discount to the compounders": the compounders' own multiples (18x to 21x) are the rate-sensitive part, and a Riksbank cycle lowers the anchor as well as widening the discount.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The counter-case is the AddLife path: a thinly covered, 100%-buy, upgrade-driven stock can run to the top of its range within a year once the evidence arrives, and 19x on a stock compounding EPS at 16% is a P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio near 1.2, not a mania. Two quarters of drop-through, with the acquisition engine on pace and leverage falling, would move my fair multiple to 17x to 18x. A Riksbank path to 2.50% and a stronger krona would hold it at 14x to 15x whatever the company reports.

Score: 62, set by the Rater. Neutral on both measures gives C. Placed in the upper half because the peer reading leans cheap, the product-only perimeter buying at 6x deserves more than the 9x-paying past, and the memo's fair multiple is about 16x against 13.5x; held below the top of the band because a turning-up stock with uncertain reported earnings in a rising-rate regime deserves a multiple near its median, not the 19.2x guideline drawn from the 2020-22 mania.

12Total shareholder return, Dupont split, 6 to 18 months and three years

Key messageThe model's +84% return to December 2027 is about three-fifths multiple (12.9x to 19.22x) and two-fifths earnings. At the 75th-percentile multiple of 16.1x the return is +54%, and at the median of 13.3x it is +28%, which is the earnings leg alone. The guideline 19.2x belongs to a reinforcing phase and a rate regime that the stock is not yet in.

Evidence. At the guideline fair multiple of 19.22x, and from SEK 256.40, the model's total shareholder return is +84.4% (+68.7% annualised) to the 18-month column (31 December 2027), for a value of SEK 472.78 a share. To the three-year column (30 June 2029) it is +122.6% (+35.0% annualised), for a value of SEK 570.87. Dividends contribute nothing, because none is paid or modelled. The two horizons are the model's fixed columns after the last reported period, not 18 months and three years from today.

How the return is built. Today the shares trade at 12.9x the model's 24-month-forward EPS of about SEK 19.9, a blend of FY2027's SEK 18.38 and FY2028's SEK 21.32. At December 2027 the 24-month-forward EPS is FY2029's SEK 24.60, and at 19.22x that is worth SEK 472.78. The 18-month return therefore splits into three legs: earnings, as forward EPS rolls from SEK 19.9 to SEK 24.60, +24%; the multiple, from 12.9x to 19.22x, +49%; and dividends, 0. Compounded, the legs give +84%.

By June 2029 forward EPS is about SEK 29.7 (a blend of FY2030's SEK 27.96 and the model's extrapolated FY2031), 49% above today's, and the multiple leg is the same +49%; compounded, the return is +123%. The one-page summary's Dupont table labels the two legs the other way round; the products agree with mine, but I read the earnings leg as the smaller of the two at 18 months (see the end notes).

What drives it. Three-fifths of the 18-month return is the multiple moving from the median to the 90th percentile, which is the judgement in topic 11. Two-fifths is the earnings growing as forecast, which is the subject of topics 6 and 7. The earnings leg is the part I trust: it needs the FY2027 and FY2028 forecasts to be broadly right and FY2029 to be in sight, and about a third of FY2027's increase is already contracted. The multiple leg is the part I discount.

The return at other multiples. The grid below shows the December 2027 value at each multiple. Two rows matter most. At the median of 13.3x the return of about +28% is the earnings leg alone. If the acquisition engine stalls and FY2029 EPS is only about SEK 21.5 from the businesses already owned, the return is about +12% at 13.3x, flat at 11.9x and about -23% at 9.2x. The brokers' bear cases (SEK 170) and the 52-week low (SEK 164.5) sit at the bottom of that grid once a weaker pound is added.

Inference. The skew of returns over 18 months is positive at every multiple down to the ten-year 35th percentile, because the earnings leg alone is worth about +28% and erasing it would take a de-rating of about three and a half turns. A downside of -20% to -35% needs the dual shock, or a sector de-rating combined with a stalled acquisition engine. By contrast, the upside to the guideline needs everything to go right at once.

A plausible central expectation, taking 16x as the fair multiple and holding 70% confidence in the model's FY2027 EPS, is a return of about +40% to +55% to the end of 2027 and about +80% to +100% to mid-2029. The three-year figure is the one at which the earnings leg catches up with the multiple leg and the case stands on its own feet.

Market against me. The brokers' targets (SEK 313 to 342, +23% to +34%) are twelve-month targets set at about 16x to 17x our FY2027 to FY2028 earnings, and they exclude unannounced acquisitions. My 18-month view at the same multiple is higher, mainly because it rolls forward a further year of earnings and includes the acquisitions. The dashboard rates TSR against valuation at B (the memo's modal return re-based, 28 October 2026). At 13.5x, the market is pricing roughly the earnings leg and no re-rating.

Counter-case and what would change my view. The counter-case is that the multiple has ranged from 9.5x to 35.8x in five years and the regime is risk-off; a return that is three-fifths multiple is a return that is three-fifths outside the company's control. The Q4 2026 report is the first checkpoint. Cash conversion above 100% and leverage at 2.6x to 2.7x would move my central return towards the guideline line; cash conversion below 90% would move it towards the median line.

Score: 90, set by the Rater. A central return of about +47% maps to about 92-93 and the three-year check confirms it. Placed at the floor of A because about three-fifths of the return rests on a re-rating rather than earnings (the earnings leg alone is about +28%), and the lower tail is fat and correlated (a Riksbank rise and a two-turn de-rating give about -25%; the dual shock -30% to -40%).

13Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Sdiptech is a collection of good niche infrastructure businesses whose group-level record was spoiled by what it paid for acquisitions and how it financed itself, and a new management team has cleaned the group up quickly and well.

The case for the next 18 months rests on three things the company already does and one thing it has not yet done. It already grows organically (and needs to grow at only half the current rate), buys SEK 90m to 100m of EBITA a year at about 6.5x, and pays roughly flat interest. It has not yet converted growth into profit and cash at the average margin.

The earnings forecast is simple, measurable quarterly and modestly above the like-for-like sell-side forecast, through a known mechanism. Two drivers that the company reports set the centre of the forecast, and two external variables for which the company publishes sensitivities set its width.

The multiple sets the share-price outcome. Sdiptech has earned a median multiple and can reach the upper quartile on 2027's evidence, but the direction of the multiple over the next six months belongs to the Riksbank and the cohort.

The best feature of the setup is that a third of next year's EPS growth is already contracted, and the market has not written that down. The worst feature is that the single date that unlocks the acquisition engine, 10 February 2027, is also the date on which the engine could pause, and the shares have already risen 46% in nine months into a rising-rate regime.

The fundamental outcomes are skewed to the positive; the probability of guidance and sell-side upgrades is above average and dated; and the multiple's skew is negative over six months and positive over eighteen. Sdiptech is a case to size for the multiple's volatility, and to add to on the Q4 proof point rather than before it.

BThesis's Change Forces' Strength

Six strong, dated internal changes (leadership, strategy, perimeter, capital structure, standards and the acquisition restart) were delivered on time at good prices; the conversion of growth into profit and cash is still to be proved, which keeps the grade out of the top decile.

CFoundations' Robustness

Unit-level moats and margins above 20% are upper-quartile, but a 13.6% return on capital, erratic quarterly cash conversion, leverage at its ceiling, a 49% sterling exposure hedged twelve months at a time and no internal audit across 35 units make the group's foundations median.

BSetups' Fit/Crispness

A clean "Major Cause-for-Concern Clearing in a medium-quality, low-cyclicality business" has already moved the multiple from the first quartile to the median, and is handing over to a "Delivering Serial Acquirer, Mechanical EPS Upgrader" setup whose engine has run for two quarters; the fit is clean in kind and late in timing.

CCase Riskiness

The drivers are few and trackable and the business is low-cyclicality, but currency, rates, a leverage ceiling that binds for two quarters, a broken EPS beat-and-miss test and a multiple that can halve on sector events make the share price materially riskier than the operations.

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
